title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous pages Grothendieck works with 'exterior groups' (groups modulo inner automorphisms) of type (g,n), meaning discrete fundamental groups of surfaces of genus g with n punctures. He takes a type (1,1) group Pi_{1,1} (once-punctured torus, free of rank 2) with its canonical involution (the hyperelliptic involution -1). From this he forms an index-2 extension pi~ -> Z/2 with kernel pi~', and keeps track of the inertia (cusp) subgroups, of which there are 3 classes. The construction lands in a Z/2-gerbe.

This page:
1. It finishes the definition: a (Z/2Z)-gerbe is a connected groupoid whose fundamental group is Z/2Z.
2. It states the conclusion of these 'conceptual reflections'. Modulo a more careful check, there is a canonical isomorphism, defined modulo inner automorphisms:
   (70) T_{1,1}/{±1} -> S_{0,3}.
   - T_{1,1} is the full Teichmüller (extended mapping class) group of type (1,1), naturally isomorphic to GL(2,Z).
   - S_{0,3} is the 'symmetrised' group of type (0,3). It is an extension of the finite symmetry group S_3 (times Z/2 for orientation) by Pi_{0,3}, the fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,∞}.
   - Geometrically: an elliptic curve E with origin, divided by ±1, gives P^1 with one distinguished point (the image of 0) and three unordered points (the images of the 2-torsion). So M_{1,1} is identified with the universal curve of type (0,3) modulo S_3, that is M_{0,4}/S_3, as the next page makes explicit in (71)-(73).
   - On the orientation-preserving part this is the classical PSL(2,Z) ≅ (Γ(2)/±1) ⋊ S_3, with Γ(2)/±1 ≅ F_2 ≅ Pi_{0,3}. This is the Legendre λ-line covering the j-line with group S_3.
3. A marginal note refines this: the ambiguity can be reduced to inner automorphisms of S^±_{0,3} coming from Pi_{0,3}. This indeterminacy comes exactly from choosing an isomorphism between L(Pi_{1,1}) and Pi_{0,3}. Here L(Pi_{1,1}) is the type (0,3) group functorially attached to the type (1,1) group via the quotient by -1.
4. He stresses that this fact is independent of whether the natural map T_{1,1} -> GL(2,Z) is an isomorphism. One may harmlessly identify T_{1,1} with GL(2,Z). It is more hazardous to identify S_{0,3} with T_{1,1}/±1 = PGL(2,Z) when S_{0,3} is known only as an exterior group, because of the inner-automorphism ambiguity in (70).

The purpose is to compare the two basic 'modular' Teichmüller groups (1,1) and (0,3)/(0,4) canonically. This is part of the variations on the loop equation and the Galois / Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No mathematical error. The claimed isomorphism PGL(2,Z) ≅ (extension of S_3×Z/2 by F_2) and PSL(2,Z) ≅ F_2 ⋊ S_3 are correct.
Grothendieck himself flags the argument as needing 'une vérification plus soignée'.
The canonicity is only up to inner automorphisms, as he notes.

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism T_{1,1}/{±1} ≅ S_{0,3} (PGL(2,Z) as the symmetrised fundamental group of P^1-{0,1,∞} extended by S_3×Z/2), obtained via the hyperelliptic quotient / Z/2-gerbe
ideas.modern_name: PSL(2,Z) ≅ Γ(2)/±1 ⋊ S_3; M_{1,1} ≅ M_{0,4}/S_3 (Legendre family); relation Γ_{1,1}/hyperelliptic ≅ Γ_{0,[4]} with one point fixed
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre/Jacobi/Klein). In the GT setting used by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the (1,1) and (0,4) Teichmüller groups and the modular tower in general terms

ideas.what: Precise bookkeeping of the indeterminacy: the isomorphism is canonical modulo inner automorphisms coming from Pi_{0,3}, the ambiguity arising from the choice of iso L(Pi_{1,1}) ≅ Pi_{0,3}; warning against identifying S_{0,3} with PGL(2,Z) at the level of exterior groups
ideas.modern_name: outer vs. genuine isomorphisms of mapping class groups; choice of tangential base points

ideas.what: Z/2-gerbe (connected groupoid with fundamental group Z/2) used to encode a type (1,1) group with its canonical involution
ideas.modern_name: orbifold / stacky quotient by the hyperelliptic involution

deep.surprise_reason: The page derives the classical relation between the (1,1) and (0,3)/(0,4) modular groups by a conceptual route and tracks inner-automorphism ambiguities carefully. The result itself is classical and has been used extensively in GT theory, so nothing here seems absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: '312' written above is the manuscript page number, not an exponent; read 'dans une (Z/2Z)-gerbe'.
'i.e. {+liée,+} une extension canonique {+3+}' should read roughly 'i.e. un groupoïde connexe admettant Z/2Z comme groupe fondamental'.
Equation label is (70), not (7d); it is referenced as (70) on the next page.
Margin should read 'en fait, on peut le préciser mod autom. int. de S^±_{0,3} provenant de Pi_{0,3}'.
'Ce fait est {dû} à fait indépendant' should be 'Ce fait est tout à fait indépendant'.
